subject: Startups
title: Survivor Bias in Benchmarks
description: Learn Survivor Bias in Benchmarks in one minute.

hook.text: Every blog says 'great startups have 20% MoM growth.' But those numbers come from survivors, not the average.

buildup.text: Survivorship bias means we study winners and ignore the thousands that tried the same tactics and failed.

discovery.text: The average startup doesn't have 20% MoM growth. Most grow slowly, plateau, and many never find traction at all.

twist.text: Using survivor benchmarks sets unrealistic expectations. Founders burn out chasing numbers that were never normal.

climax.text: Better approach: compare today's metrics to last month's. Compete with yourself, not with curated success stories.

punchline.text: Don't benchmark against survivors. Benchmark against yourself.

quiz.question: What is survivorship bias in startup benchmarks?
options: Only studying winners and ignoring failures
Tracking too many metrics at once
